name: FlashAttention-2 work partitioning: fixing warp-level underutilization
arithmetic_intensity: No change to bytes or FLOPs relative to FA-1. FA-2 is a pure scheduling fix: it removes idle tensor-core cycles caused by poor thread-block/warp partitioning and redundant shared-memory traffic, i.e. it converts achieved FLOPs/s toward the FLOPs the tiles already imply. The metric that moves is MMA utilization (percent of tensor-core peak), not arithmetic intensity. Recorded as custom_kernel because the mechanism is kernel-organization, not an operation class.
scales_with: num_SMs (partitioning determines whether all SMs get equal work)
workarounds: Parallelize over batch * seqlen * num_heads rather than the FA-1 partitioning, so every CTA gets work without idle warps
Reduce non-tensor-core work per warp: fewer softmax rescale passes and less shared-memory round tripping between the MMA and softmax phases
Separate the intra-warpgroup and inter-warpgroup GEMM/softmax loops so tensor cores are never waiting on the SFU path
Smaller head-dim handling (up to 256) so the same SMEM budget gives more warps
notes:
FA-1 reached only 25-40% of peak FLOPS/s according to the existing prefill-attention record's source chain; FA-2's stated target was roughly 2x and the changelog calls it 'Complete rewrite, 2x faster' (author claim, 2.0). Where FA-2 does NOT apply: it is Ampere-and-later only (README: Ampere, Ada or Hopper for the CUDA path, Turing via a separate repo with a feature subset), and on ROCm it ships two different backends (composable_kernel as default, plus a Triton/aiter backend) with different GPU support lists (MI200x/MI250x/MI300x/MI355x and RDNA 3/4 for the CK backend). That is the first place the same model gets different kernels per arch. Inference-relevant additions: 2.2 splits the KV-cache load across thread blocks for tiny query lengths with a separate combine kernel, 2.5 added paged KV cache, 2.6 softcapping for Gemma-2/Grok.
